blocks.markdown: **Competitive bidding is the baseline modality**; alternative modalities are permitted **only when the statutory conditions and procedures are satisfied**. Know both the **name and the reason it can be used**, not just the vocabulary.

table.caption: The eleven NGPA modes listed in the syllabus
columns: When it applies / issue to spot
rows: Competitive bidding (Sec. 27)
Open, competitive procedure; default starting point absent a lawful basis for a different modality.
Limited source bidding (Sec. 28)
Only a limited number of known suppliers can supply a highly specialized requirement under the prescribed conditions.
Competitive dialogue (Sec. 29)
Used where the entity needs dialogue with qualified participants to develop suitable solutions for a complex requirement; follow the exact procedural safeguards.
Unsolicited offer with bid matching (Sec. 30)
A proponent submits an offer under a statutory framework that includes the right/process of matching; not a general license to bypass competition.
Direct contracting (Sec. 31)
A direct procurement mode available only on prescribed grounds (e.g., proprietary/specialized supply situations as detailed in the law/IRR).
Direct acquisition (Sec. 32)
A distinct statutory mode. Do not collapse it into direct contracting; quote the Act/IRR's separate conditions.
Repeat order (Sec. 33)
Repeat procurement of the same/similar items from the original supplier, subject to statutory limits and conditions.
Small value procurement (Sec. 34)
For procurement below the applicable threshold and under required procedural safeguards. Use the current threshold in the applicable IRR.
Negotiated procurement (Sec. 35)
Allowed only for specified situations listed by law; state the triggering ground.
Direct sales (Sec. 36)
Separate mode expressly enumerated by the NGPA; identify the statutory scenario rather than importing an older regime.
Direct procurement for science, technology and innovation (Sec. 37)
Special mode for qualified STI-related procurement under its statutory conditions.

blocks.markdown: **Exam trap: name is not authority.** A procuring entity cannot choose a noncompetitive mode just because it is faster or preferred. Identify the **statutory ground, supporting record, required approvals/notice and any applicable limits**. Thresholds and procedures should be taken from the **current NGPA IRR, not recalled from old RA 9184 notes**.
**Recall:** know all **eleven modes** listed in the syllabus and their **section numbers**.

description: Competitive bidding as baseline and the ten alternative modalities: triggers, conditions, and the name-is-not-authority trap.
